status: LOCKED at the plan_072 ledger entry
honest_framing: v0.67.0's hybrid H added nothing over the textbook learner and timed out on EJ and GB. What did work, observed but not gated, was arm B = brute.certify/32h (v0.66.0, unchanged): under a memory cap it decided 4 of 5 real decoders at true+1 in 808-3670 steps against 3533-13269 / 11469 for the textbook learner. This study tests that observation honestly on NEW real software: 8 more CPython incremental decoders, fresh seeds, two seeds each, with a ground truth that is NOT hand-written but derived by an independent oracle (BFS over real decoder getstate() values + Moore minimisation; it reproduces all 5 hand-written v0.64-0.67 truths). No brute/ code changes. The guarantee is conditional on the declared N (here true+1, a generous declaration), clean readings, and no resets.
question: Does Brute's existing SAT engine (certify/32h, unchanged) decide new real decoders reset-free at a tight N, soundly, with fewer decoder steps than the textbook learner (baseline/32t, unchanged)?
heldout: HK (big5hkscs) is held out: no run of any arm touched it before the freeze
target_software: experiments/targets_072.py: real CPython 3.13.5 incremental decoders (shift_jis, euc_kr, big5, utf-32-le, utf-8-sig, utf-16-be, euc_jis_2004, big5hkscs) on 3 byte values each; one decoder object per job, no reset, 2-bit readings (non-empty, contains U+FFFD); same interface rules as experiments/targets_070.py

truth.file: experiments/truth_072.json built by scripts/make_truth_072.py (refuses overwrite; ledger event truth_072 before any run)
truth.method: oracle independent of Brute: BFS over decoder states identified by decoder.getstate() plus the last reading, then Moore partition refinement. getstate() is used only by the truth script, never by the runner's adapter
truth.validation: the same oracle on the five v0.64-0.67 targets (U3, U4, W16, EJ, GB) is Moore-equivalent from the start state to the hand-written truth_069 on all five (checked in tests)
truth.note: U32 (42 reachable states), U8S (initial BOM states are never revisited), U16B (21) and EJ4 (13) have transient or non-minimal structure; the Moore minimum is what N is compared with

api.T: brute.baseline/32t unchanged (textbook Rivest-Schapire homing + L* + Vasilevskii-Chow)

design.jobs: plus1: B and T x 8 targets x seeds 12720101, 12720102 = 32 jobs; plus3 (diagnostic, ungated): B x 8 targets x seed 12720101 = 8 jobs; 40 jobs. Smoke seed 12720301 (SJ, KR, plus1, B and T) is not gated
design.memory: each job's child sets RLIMIT_AS = 1.8 GiB and oom_score_adj 1000 (runner-side, not in brute/). MemoryError or a signal exit -> KILL record (cap_hit true/false). 3 workers. The box had about 2.7-5 GB of available RAM at the v0.67.0 run; no job was killed by the kernel then
design.time: SIGKILL at 240 s -> KILL record; main cap 2400 s; the main run happens once

gates.GHEAD72: HEADLINE: arm B decided (IDF, recounted correct) on at least 12 of the 16 plus1 cells, 0 WRONG, and the held-out HK decided on at least 1 of its 2 seeds
gates.GSTEP72: over plus1 (target, seed) cells where B and T both decided, the median of B decoder steps / T decoder steps is at most 0.5 (v0.67.0 observed 0.11-0.32 on 4 targets, not gated)
gates.GS72_sound: 0 WRONG among decided records of B (plus1 and plus3) and of T
gates.GBASE72: all 16 plus1 T records present and recounted; the B/T table is written; T is the comparison, not gated beyond presence
gates.GNORESET72: adapter AST has no reset, getstate, setstate, buffer or private use; getincrementaldecoder is called once in Target.__init__; every non-KILL record has resets 0 and decoder_objects 1
gates.GFID72: every non-KILL record's action sequence replayed on one fresh decoder gives exactly the recorded readings
gates.GMEM72: every record has rlimit_as_bytes 1.8 GiB and workers 3; any cap hit appears as a KILL record
gates.GHOST72: brute/ is byte-identical to tag v0.67.0 (empty git diff at run_start): no engine change in this version
gates.GTRUTH72: scripts/make_truth_072.py --check reproduces experiments/truth_072.json; ledger event truth_072 precedes the run; its sha matches
gates.GLIVE72: the main run sealed complete within the main cap
gates.G_PROC72: commit chain plan < build_authorization < freeze < run_start < seal

diagnostic_not_gated: B at plus3 (one seed per target): decided count and steps are reported in the table. At N 12 in v0.66.0 B was IDU or out of memory, so failure here is expected for larger targets and is not a gate
status_rule: Release v0.68.0 either way. Every gate is reported; failures are published, never forced
recount: truth_072 simulation: B IDF correct iff the model at s1 is Moore-equivalent to the truth at its final state (ID additionally needs every start-consistent state equivalent to truth start); T ID correct iff its hypothesis is equivalent to the truth at origin_step; labels as scripts/recount_070.label with truth_072
what_this_cannot_show: No noise; real decoders only; sizes 3-11 states; N = true+1 is generous (the truth sizes come from the oracle, not from a-priori knowledge); two seeds per cell; the truth oracle shares CPython with the targets (it is independent of Brute, not of CPython); B's guarantee does not cover loose N
pre_plan_exploration: Observed before the lock: the oracle was run on the 8 targets and on the 5 old targets to read sizes and validate against the hand truth. No Brute arm ran on any new target
